text:
Jackson LaCombe is playing 26:49 a night for Anaheim, up from 24:15, and running the power play nearly every time the Ducks get one. The points have followed: 25 in 22 games, 16 on the power play, and 24 of them assists.

The even-strength numbers are the warning light. The Ducks get just 38% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 11 points worse than without him, and they've scored 9.7 more goals than those chances deserve while he's out there. That cushion fades. He's scoring 2.54 points per 60 minutes against a talent range we put at 1.61 to 2.17, so some of this pace is borrowed.

The tools are real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 46th of 215 defensemen last season. The question is whether a heavier workload is helping Anaheim or just giving the opponents more looks.
headline: LaCombe carries Anaheim's minutes, and its power play
